en.Alphabet: A finite set of allowed symbols.
en.String: A finite ordered sequence of symbols.
en.Specification: A rule stating allowed inputs and required outputs.
en.Union: Accept a string from either alternative.
en.Kleene star: Zero or more concatenated members of a language.
en.State: A finite summary of the processed prefix.
en.Invariant: A statement preserved after every transition.
en.Accepting state: A state that accepts if input has ended there.
en.Nondeterminism: A transition may offer several possible next states.
en.Epsilon move: A state change that consumes no input symbol.
en.Existential acceptance: One finite successful complete run suffices.
en.Subset state: One DFA state representing several possible NFA states.
en.Epsilon closure: All states reachable without consuming symbols, including the starting set.
en.Sink: A state whose every transition returns to itself.
en.Generalized edge: An edge labelled by a regular expression.
en.Elimination: Removing a state while preserving all possible surviving routes.
en.Loop: A route from a state back to itself.
en.Backtracking: Undo a choice and try an alternative path.
en.Active set: All states reachable after the current input prefix.
en.Preprocessing: Work performed before a particular input is matched.
en.Product state: A pair recording one state of each machine.
en.Symmetric difference: Strings belonging to exactly one of two languages.
en.Reachability: Whether a finite path leads from the start to a state.
en.Pigeonhole principle: More objects than categories force two objects into one category.
en.Distinguishing suffix: The same appended string creates different required membership answers.
en.Nonregular: No finite automaton recognizes the language.
en.Nonterminal: A named component that still needs rewriting.
en.Terminal: A symbol allowed in the finished string.
en.Derivation: A sequence of rule applications starting at the start variable.
en.Parse tree: A hierarchy showing which grammar rules build the string.
en.Precedence: A rule deciding which operator groups more tightly.
en.Associativity: How repeated operators at the same level group.
en.CNF: Grammar rules restricted to two variables or one terminal, with a protected start exception.
en.Unit production: A rule A→B containing a single variable on the right.
en.Span: A contiguous substring between two boundaries.
en.Dynamic programming: Store shorter subproblem answers and reuse them in larger problems.
en.Half-open interval: Include the start position and exclude the end position.
en.Configuration: Current state, head position and tape contents together.
en.Tape alphabet: All symbols that may be written, including blank and markers.
en.Transition: One rule that reads, writes, moves and changes state.
en.Marker: A tape symbol recording that a position has been processed.
en.Phase: A group of steps serving one clearly stated purpose.
en.Termination measure: A nonnegative quantity that strictly decreases during repeated progress.
en.Transition table: A list of rules, one row for each pair of state and symbol read, giving the new state, the symbol to write and the move.
en.State diagram: A drawing with a circle for each state and an arrow for each rule, labelled read/write,move.
en.Multitrack tape: One tape and one head, where each cell holds one symbol for every track.
en.Multitape machine: A machine with several tapes, each with its own head, all controlled by one state.
en.Equivalent models: Two models that recognize the same languages and compute the same functions, even if one is slower.
en.Encoding: A finite string representing a machine or input.
en.Universal machine: One interpreter able to simulate encoded machines.
en.Simulation overhead: Extra work needed to reproduce another model’s steps.
en.Recognizer: Accepts every member and never accepts a nonmember; it may loop on nonmembers.
en.Decider: Gives a correct membership answer and halts on every input.
en.Witness: A finite object that establishes a yes answer.
en.Undecidable: No algorithm always halts with the correct answer for every allowed input.
en.Diagonalization: Use a construction’s own description to force disagreement.
en.Total algorithm: An algorithm guaranteed to halt on every input in its domain.
en.Dovetailing: Share steps fairly among simulations so none waits forever for another.
en.Complement: All allowed input strings outside the language.
en.Acceptance flag: A remembered fact that a simulation has already accepted.
en.Reduction: A computable rewrite that turns a question about one language into a question about another.
en.Hypothetical decider: A decider that we assume exists only so that we can derive a contradiction from it.
en.Encoding ⟨M⟩: A string that describes machine M, so that another machine can take it as input.
en.Closure property: A class of languages is closed under an operation if applying the operation to members always gives a member.
en.Gadget: The fixed piece of machine behavior that the construction wraps around M and w.
en.Truth assignment: A choice of true or false for each atomic proposition.
en.Satisfiable: True for at least one assignment.
en.Equivalence: Agreement in truth value on every assignment.
en.Converse: The reversed implication Q→P of P→Q.
en.Literal: An atom or the negation of one atom.
en.Clause: A disjunction of literals, such as p∨¬q.
en.Premise: A statement temporarily assumed true when checking an argument.
en.Countermodel: An assignment with every premise true and conclusion false.
en.Entailment: A conclusion true in every model of the premises.
en.Domain: The nonempty collection of objects variables may name.
en.Scope: The part of a formula governed by a quantifier or connective.
en.Quantifier extraction: Moving a quantifier from inside part of a formula out to the front, without changing the meaning.
en.Free variable: A variable that no quantifier around it captures, so its value must come from outside.
en.Counter-model: A small model in which one formula is true and another is false, showing they are not equivalent.
en.Prenex form: A formula with all quantifiers at the front and no quantifier inside the rest of the formula.

zh.字母表: 由允许使用的符号组成的有限集合。
zh.字符串: 由符号组成的有限的有序序列。
zh.规格: 说明允许的输入和要求的输出的一条规则。
zh.并: 接受来自任意一个选择的字符串。
zh.连接: 把一个字符串放在另一个字符串后面。
zh.Kleene 星: 把一个语言中的成员连接零次或多次。
zh.状态: 对已处理前缀的有限摘要。
zh.不变量: 在每次转移之后都保持成立的陈述。
zh.接受状态: 如果输入恰好在这里结束，就接受的状态。
zh.非确定性: 一次转移可以提供多个可能的下一状态。
zh.ε 转移: 不消耗任何输入符号的状态改变。
zh.存在性接受: 只要有一次有限的、完整的、成功的运行就够了。
zh.子集状态: 一个 DFA 状态，它表示几个可能的 NFA 状态。
zh.ε 闭包: 不消耗符号就能到达的所有状态，包括起始的那个集合本身。
zh.汇点: 每一个转移都回到自身的状态。
zh.广义边: 用正则表达式标记的边。
zh.消除: 移除一个状态，同时保留所有幸存端点之间可能的路线。
zh.自环: 从一个状态回到它自己的路线。
zh.回溯: 撤销一个选择，并尝试另一条路径。
zh.活跃集合: 当前输入前缀之后所有可达的状态。
zh.预处理: 在匹配某个具体输入之前所做的工作。
zh.积状态: 记录两台机器各自一个状态的有序对。
zh.对称差: 恰好属于两个语言之一的字符串。
zh.可达性: 是否存在一条有限的路径，从起点通向某个状态。
zh.抽屉原理: 对象的个数多于类别的个数时，必定有两个对象落入同一个类别。
zh.区分后缀: 追加同一个字符串之后，所要求的成员资格答案却不同。
zh.非正则: 没有任何有限自动机能识别该语言。
zh.非终结符: 仍然需要被重写的有名字的组件。
zh.终结符: 允许出现在最终字符串中的符号。
zh.推导: 从起始变量开始的一系列规则应用。
zh.解析树: 一个层级结构，显示是哪些文法规则构造出了这个字符串。
zh.优先级: 决定哪个运算符结合得更紧的规则。
zh.结合性: 同一层级上重复出现的运算符如何分组。
zh.Chomsky 范式: 规则被限制为两个变量或一个终结符，另有一个受保护的起始符号例外。
zh.可空: 一个变量能推导出 ε。
zh.单位产生式: 右侧只有一个变量的规则 A→B。
zh.片段: 两个边界之间的连续子串。
zh.动态规划: 存储较短子问题的答案，并在更大的问题中重复使用它们。
zh.左闭右开区间: 包含起始位置，不包含结束位置。
zh.配置: 当前状态、读写头位置和纸带内容合在一起。
zh.带字母表: 所有可以被写入的符号，包括空白和标记。
zh.转移: 一条读取、写入、移动并改变状态的规则。
zh.标记: 记录某个位置已经被处理过的纸带符号。
zh.阶段: 为了一个清楚陈述的目的而服务的一组步骤。
zh.终止度量: 在重复推进的过程中严格递减的一个非负量。
zh.转移规则表: 一张规则列表，为每对（状态，读到的符号）列一行，给出新状态、要写的符号和移动方向。
zh.状态图: 一幅图，每个状态一个圆，每条规则一条箭头，标签写成 读/写,移动。
zh.多轨带: 一条带、一个磁头，每个格子为每条轨道存放一个符号。
zh.多带机器: 有几条带的机器，每条带有自己的磁头，由同一个状态控制。
zh.等价模型: 识别同样的语言、计算同样的函数的两种模型，即使其中一个更慢。
zh.编码: 表示一台机器或一个输入的有限字符串。
zh.通用机器: 一个能够模拟被编码机器的解释器。
zh.模拟开销: 重现另一个模型的各个步骤所需要的额外工作。
zh.识别器: 接受每一个成员，并且从不接受非成员；它可以在非成员上循环。
zh.判定器: 对每一个输入都给出正确的成员资格答案，并且停机。
zh.见证: 能够确立“是”这个答案的一个有限对象。
zh.不可判定: 没有任何算法能对每一个允许的输入都停机，并给出正确的答案。
zh.对角化: 利用所构造对象自身的描述，迫使它与某个东西产生分歧。
zh.全停机算法: 保证在其定义域内的每一个输入上都会停机的算法。
zh.交错模拟: 在各个模拟之间公平地分配步数，使得没有哪一个会永远等待另一个。
zh.补语言: 所有不属于该语言的允许输入字符串。
zh.接受标志: 记住的一个事实：某个模拟已经接受了。
zh.归约: 一种可计算的改写，把关于一个语言的问题变成关于另一个语言的问题。
zh.假想的判定器: 我们只是为了推出矛盾而假设存在的判定器。
zh.编码 ⟨M⟩: 描述机器 M 的一个串，使别的机器可以把它当作输入。
zh.封闭性: 如果对一类语言中的成员施行某种运算，结果总还在这一类里，就说这类语言对该运算封闭。
zh.构造件: 构造过程中包在 M 和 w 外面的那一小段固定的机器行为。
zh.真值赋值: 为每个原子命题选定真或者假。
zh.等价: 在每一个赋值下，真值都一致。
zh.逆命题: P→Q 被反转之后的蕴含 Q→P。
zh.逆否命题: 蕴含 ¬Q→¬P，它与 P→Q 等价。
zh.文字: 一个原子命题，或者一个原子命题的否定。
zh.子句: 若干文字的析取，例如 p∨¬q。
zh.合取范式: 若干子句的合取；每一个子句都必须成立。
zh.前提: 在检验一个论证时，暂时假定为真的陈述。
zh.反模型: 使每个前提都为真而结论为假的赋值。
zh.蕴涵: 在前提的每一个模型中都为真的结论。
zh.论域: 变量可以指称的对象所组成的非空集合。
zh.作用域: 公式中受某个量词或联结词支配的那一部分。
zh.量词提取: 把量词从公式某个部分的内部移到最前面，而不改变含义。
zh.自由变量: 周围没有量词捕获的变量，它的取值必须从外部给定。
zh.前束范式: 所有量词都在最前面，其余部分不再含有量词的公式。
